characterization_methods.key_findings: All values plotted represent averages of three measurements for every material state.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)
hardness screening as a function of alloy composition and aging treatment

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

interfaces.phase_evolution: nm-sized κ-carbides form during aging; pronounced strengthening with high Al (~8 wt.%).

phase_interfaces.coherence: coherent; lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace; successively filled from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10×50×130 mm³ blocks were hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets; sheets were reheated to 1100 °C and water quenched.
Aging conducted in air at 600 °C for 1 h, then oil quenched.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: averages of three measurements for every material state

precipitates.coherency: coherent; lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to the austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix; cuboidal nanoprecipitates
precipitates.type: κ-carbide (L'1₂ ordered fcc; approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)₃AlC; non-oxide perovskite)

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized austenitic microstructure (grain size ~20 µm) with nm-sized κ-carbide precipitates formed during aging, plus some retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: For the alloy Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al, aging for 1 h leads to an increase in YS, UTS, and hardness (increasing with temperature) and only to a minor reduction in TE [b0024].

High Al content (~8 wt.%) results in pronounced strengthening during aging, attributed to the formation of nm-sized κ-carbides during aging; κ-carbides are thermally very stable at 600 °C and prevail after 100 h heat treatment with only modest coarsening [b0025].

For Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al without aging, the mechanical response is similar to that of the Al-free alloy; only a minor change in YS (increase), UTS, and TE (decrease) is found (as-homogenized baseline context) [b0024].

In austenitic steels strengthened by regularly arranged nanosized κ-carbides (illustrated in Fig. 5 for the 24 h/600 °C condition), the prevalent deformation mechanism is Orowan bypassing of longitudinal κ-carbide rods with expansion of dislocation loops assisted by dislocation cross-slip and, to a minor extent, shearing of κ-carbides [b0032].
